nodes.label: Lazy Read Core (LazyDicomReader)
nodes.rationale: Backs DicomMessage.readFile since 1.0: parseDicom records offsets only, wrap is O(#elements) with no decoding, entries materialize on first access. Only transfer syntax and SpecificCharacterSet are resolved eagerly at wrap time because everything else depends on them. No behavioral cliff, only deferred work.

nodes.label: Getter-Backed Lazy Entry
nodes.rationale: Same observable shape as a 0.x eager entry ({vr, Value, _rawValue}) but Value/_rawValue are accessors: getter materializes and caches on first access; setter stores the value and flips the non-enumerable _dirty flag (plus nested-dirt counters) — the seam the passthrough writer is built on.

nodes.label: Wrap-Time Character Set Resolution
nodes.rationale: There is no scan in the lazy model, so the decoder is resolved once per dataset at wrap time instead of mid-scan swapping; sequence items get per-item contexts, which actually exceeds the 0.x single-charset-per-file reader.

nodes.label: Whole-File Eager Fallback
nodes.rationale: When the tokenizer rejects the stream outright (truncation, declared-length overruns, missing part-10 plumbing) the entire read is delegated to the eager core so malformed real-world files behave exactly as they always have — errors and ignoreErrors recovery points reproduced by running the eager reader itself.

nodes.label: Eager Read Core (DCMJS_CORE=eager escape hatch)
nodes.rationale: A beta-soak escape hatch, not a supported long-term mode; slated for deletion in 1.x once the async reader is re-platformed onto the tokenizer. Kept so any lazy-core difference can be bisected against 0.x behavior.

nodes.label: Documented Lazy-vs-Eager Divergences
nodes.rationale: Three intentional, test-pinned divergences: (1) value-level errors surface at first access instead of during readFile; (2) ignoreErrors:true returns the full dict with only the failing entry undefined — strictly more informative than eager truncation; (3) charset scope applies per dataset/item rather than per stream position, diverging only on non-conformant ordering.
